objective: Persist complete immutable FOOD-005J payable-assessment versions at exact assessment identity/version after authenticating their exact durable physical-order association. Preserve ordered adjustments, arithmetic, provenance and consecutive revision history without selecting a currently payable assessment or conferring payment, policy or operational authority.

No authoritative durable payable-assessment table, write adapter or exact-read owner exists at the baseline.
existingNonOwners: FOOD-005J is a pure immutable assessment domain and arithmetic validator.
FOOD-005K is a pure projection consuming exact assessment plus transient normalized payment evidence; it performs no persistence.
FOOD-005Q proves exact authorized-charge inclusion; it does not record the assessment.
FOOD-005R validates supplied exact assessment-selection evidence; it is not durable assessment storage or automatic currentness.
FOOD-005S composes charge-policy satisfaction, not assessment persistence or checkout readiness.

FOOD-008C/008D and FOOD-008E/008F persist/read electronic and cash evidence respectively, not payable assessments. Commerce RiverOrder persistence uses a different identity/model and is not a FOOD-005J owner.

roles.FOOD-005E/008A/008B: Canonical physical-order values, immutable durable parent and readFoodPhysicalOrderVersionByExactIdentity.
roles.FOOD-008A: Canonical snapshot storage, lifecycle insertion guards, primary identity and immutable trigger precedent.
roles.FOOD-008C/008E: Injected D1 prepare/bind/all, five persistence outcomes, capture before await, immutable evidence, exact replay and one uncertain-insert reread. Their version-1-only restrictions are not copied to assessments.
roles.FOOD-008D/008F: Separate public exact historical read ownership; neither authenticates assessment values.
roles.FOOD-005K: Downstream arithmetic projection; not invoked or persisted here.

identity.creator: createFoodPayableAssessmentId
identity.rule: Primitive canonical string; nonempty local component, no colon in local component, no surrounding whitespace. No generated identity, trimming or prefix repair.

order.meaning: Exact FoodPhysicalOrderId plus exact order version and its historical merchandise subtotal, not the full order snapshot.

adjustments.references: reference and sourceReference are primitive canonical nonempty strings of at most 512 UTF-16 code units. reference is unique within one assessment version across both directions. sourceReference is provenance, not proof of policy authorization.
adjustments.duplicates: Same reference repeated, even across charge and credit, is invalid. Equal amounts or shared sourceReference with distinct references are permitted; no global charge/source uniqueness is inferred.
adjustments.replacementOnRevision: The supplied collection replaces the previous collection; it is not appended automatically. No sorting, merging, inference or deduplication.

money.currency: Primitive string matching existing /^[A-Z]{3}$/; no lowercase coercion and no new ISO-code allowlist. All adjustment money and amountDue use the exact merchandiseSubtotal currency.
money.minorUnits: Primitive nonnegative safe-integer number, at most 9007199254740991; finite by safe-integer validation. No decimal-unit conversion, Number coercion, rounding or floating-point repricing.
money.negativeZero: The existing validator admits numeric -0 as zero. Preserve domain semantics: canonical JSON.stringify emits 0. Do not invent a business distinction for signed zero; durable noncanonical -0 text fails exact reserialization.
money.arithmetic: Use validateFoodPayableAssessmentVersion, not a competing calculator. It separately safe-adds subtotal plus all charges and the sum of all credits, rejects either intermediate overflow, rejects credits exceeding gross, and requires supplied amountDue to equal gross minus credits. A net result within range does not excuse an unsafe gross or credit sum.

assessment.textBounds: attribution and sourceReference: primitive nonempty canonical strings, maximum 512 UTF-16 code units
assessment.assessedOn: Existing validateFoodReviewDate: supplied calendar-valid YYYY-MM-DD. No clock, generated persistence timestamp, timezone conversion or inferred assessor authentication.

domainContract.amountDueVersusSubtotal: amountDue is derived by domain creation/revision from subtotal and explicit adjustments; complete candidate validation accepts it only when exact arithmetic agrees. It can equal, exceed, fall below, or be zero relative to subtotal. Never substitute subtotal for amountDue.

versions.supported: Every positive primitive safe-integer assessment version from 1 through Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER is structurally supported; unlike electronic/cash evidence, version greater than 1 is not inherently invalid.
versions.revision: reviseFoodPayableAssessmentVersion validates the previous snapshot, requires stable assessment ID, previous.version < Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, next.version exactly previous.version + 1, and the same exact order ID/version. Adjustments and assessment metadata may change. No monotonic-date rule or delta-only changes are introduced.
versions.historicalValidation: validateFoodPayableAssessmentVersion authenticates an individual full snapshot without previous versions. This proves structural/arithmetic validity, not that it was a legal consecutive transition. New durable revision insertion requires exact predecessor evidence and SQL guards.
versions.newOrderVersion: A different physical-order version requires a new assessment ID. Multiple distinct assessment IDs for one exact order remain allowed; there is no one-assessment-per-order constraint.
versions.noImportGaps: No inserting absent version 5 into empty storage merely because its standalone snapshot validates. Historical existing versions remain replayable even after later revisions. Bulk history import is outside this API.

domainContract.immutability: Existing validators build detached frozen root, order, money, ordered adjustment array/items and assessment metadata. Do not mutate domain modules or freeze caller/database objects in place.

columnsInOrder.name: order_version
columnsInOrder.meaning: exact durable physical-order version 1 or 2 under 008A/008B

columnsInOrder.name: snapshot_format_version
columnsInOrder.meaning: exactly 1 for this proposed serialization contract

columnsInOrder.name: snapshot_json
columnsInOrder.meaning: canonical complete FoodPayableAssessmentVersion including identity, order, all adjustments, amountDue and provenance

storage.moneyColumnEvaluation: Separate subtotal currency/minorUnits and amountDue currency/minorUnits columns were evaluated and rejected here: no owned SQL amount query or aggregation needs them, while the validated full snapshot preserves all four scalars exactly. Do not duplicate monetary authority across columns and JSON without a future query requirement. Their absence is a storage design choice, not omission from the persisted value.
storage.chosenReason: Bounded ordered adjustments and provenance are one immutable aggregate. One INSERT stores the whole snapshot atomically; one row reconstructs it consistently, avoiding child-row batching or unsupported transaction assumptions. Identity/order columns support exact lookup, revision guards and parent reference constraints. Format version makes future evolution explicit without weakening existing readers.

rejectedAlternatives.reason: Requires atomic parent/ordered-child insertion and joins with an injection surface that currently guarantees only individual statements. Adds partial-aggregate and consistency risks without a required SQL adjustment query.
Weakens direct primary identity, stable-order SQL guards and exact foreign-key constraints.
Destroys immutable historical revisions, replay classification and exact-version authority.

rejectedAlternatives.model: generic payment entity or reuse electronic/cash table
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Assessments describe amount due, not received/confirmed funds; separate source-family contracts must remain intact.

constraints: All six columns NOT NULL in a STRICT SQLite table or equivalent explicit storage-class checks; exact binary text key semantics.
PRIMARY KEY (assessment_id, assessment_version). No unique order_id/order_version or sourceReference constraint.
assessment_version integer BETWEEN 1 AND 9007199254740991; order_version integer IN (1,2); snapshot_format_version exactly integer 1.

assessment_id bounded nonempty text with FOOD-005J prefix/local maximum 200; order_id bounded nonempty text with FOOD-005E prefix/local maximum 128. SQL length checks supplement domain parsing and do not redefine JavaScript UTF-16 bounds or Unicode normalization.

snapshot_json nonempty TEXT containing valid JSON object. Use CASE guarding json_type with json_valid where needed so malformed text cannot bypass checks or cause unintended evaluation-order assumptions. SQL JSON validity does not replace canonical domain authentication.

Composite FOREIGN KEY (order_id, order_version) REFERENCES food_physical_order_versions(order_id, order_version), with no cascades or parent changes. Match the 0009 composite-reference precedent; 0010 omits it, so this is an explicit new contract choice, not a claim all FOOD tables already require one.

A BEFORE INSERT order guard rejects absence of the exact parent row using EXISTS with both coordinates. It supplements the FK and runtime authentication without parsing or mutating the order snapshot.

A BEFORE INSERT initial guard rejects NEW.assessment_version = 1 when any row for NEW.assessment_id already exists. Exact replay still resolves by private pre-read or race reread; the trigger does not perform overwrite semantics.

A BEFORE INSERT revision guard rejects NEW.assessment_version > 1 unless a row exists with assessment_id = NEW.assessment_id, assessment_version = NEW.assessment_version - 1, order_id = NEW.order_id and order_version = NEW.order_version. No MAX or latest query is needed.
BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers always RAISE(ABORT), using existing FOOD immutable-trigger style. No REPLACE, UPSERT, ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, backfill or schema mutation of existing tables.
storage.schemaAuthorityLimit: SQL enforces identity, atomic predecessor/exact-parent existence, stable order coordinates and immutability, not the full JSON business arithmetic or assessor authority. Complete domain/canonical authentication belongs to the adapter; direct database access is a separate trust boundary.
storage.deploymentPrerequisites: Before any separately authorized integration, verify actual 0008 parent schema, SQLite STRICT/JSON/trigger support and foreign-key enforcement on the runtime connection. Existing 0009/0010 file presence does not prove application. This authoring task creates no migration and executes none.

canonicalSerialization.payload: Full domain object; unlike 008A's column-excluding snapshot, include id/version/order coordinates deliberately and require equality with all duplicated durable columns. This makes standalone domain reconstruction explicit and preserves a single complete assessment value.
canonicalSerialization.build: First safely capture and validate the complete candidate. Construct fresh explicit objects and a dense adjustments array from the validator-produced value in the locked key orders. Serialize once with JSON.stringify without replacer or whitespace. Retain original adjustment order and exact text; never sort or collapse equal amounts/references.
canonicalSerialization.numbers: Primitive finite safe-integer numeric values only. Runtime JSON.stringify defines canonical decimal/escape representation; no strings, bigint JSON values, fractions, NaN, Infinity, numeric coercion or alternate arbitrary-precision money format. Follow domain zero semantics.
canonicalSerialization.keys: All listed keys are required with own data descriptors. No additional keys, symbols, accessors, inherited substitutes, custom prototypes, undefined, null, sparse arrays or repair. Arbitrary JSON parse success is insufficient.
canonicalSerialization.inputVersusStoredOrdering: Caller object own-key insertion order may differ; capture by declared fields and serialize the validated value. Caller adjustment element order is preserved. Stored root/nested key ordering, array ordering, number spelling and escaping must already match the canonical string exactly.
canonicalSerialization.reconstruct: Authenticate exact own-data row shape and primitive coordinates/format/string, JSON.parse safely, authenticate exact recursive payload shape, then run validateFoodPayableAssessmentVersion. Require payload id/version/order.id/order.version strictly equal row columns and requested coordinates. Rebuild canonical JSON from the validated value and require generated text === stored snapshot_json. Do not normalize and accept different stored text.
canonicalSerialization.duplicateJsonMembers: Native JSON.parse can collapse duplicate keys; canonical reserialization differs from the original duplicated-member text and must reject it, even if parsed content would otherwise validate.
canonicalSerialization.roundTrip: For every accepted candidate, reconstructing its normalized row produces the same complete canonical value and canonical text. Returned values are newly validator-produced and deeply frozen; raw parsed JSON, mutable row objects or caller references never escape.
canonicalSerialization.futureEvolution: Format 1 remains immutable. Future additional fields, key orders or schema versions need a separately reviewed format/migration/reader contract; never silently reinterpret historical text.
canonicalSerialization.canonicalTamperingLimit: Reordering an otherwise canonical adjustment array produces a different valid historical snapshot, not necessarily malformed JSON. Compare against the requested candidate to detect conflict; standalone shape/canonical validation cannot reveal a privileged replacement with a different fully canonical value. Durable immutability/access control supplies that protection; this adapter provides no cryptographic tamper proof.

validation.candidateBeforeAwait: Strictly capture the full fixed-schema graph before any asynchronous work. Reject hostile inspection, shape, text and primitive failures as invalid with zero D1 calls. Use existing parsers/validators as business authority; shape capture does not replace domain validation.
validation.records: Object.prototype or null-prototype records only; inspect Reflect.ownKeys and own descriptors, never read an accessor-backed property. Reject unsupported symbols, missing/extra keys and inherited fields. Catch proxy inspection errors. JavaScript has no reliable universal proxy detector: validate the detached captured primitives; do not claim all proxies can be recognized without traps.
validation.arrays: Capture adjustments from an actual plain Array with an own safe integer length 0..32; only length and dense own data-index properties 0..length-1 are allowed. Reject custom prototypes, symbols, extra properties, holes, accessor slots and inherited indices before copying. Bound iteration by captured validated length.
validation.cyclesAndAliasing: Fixed record schemas and bounded depth reject cyclic structural substitutions before recursive processing. If a traversal uses cycle detection, track the active path so legitimate shared references such as reused immutable money do not become invalid. Copy shared values into detached canonical objects.
validation.domain: Invoke validateFoodPayableAssessmentVersion and require input canonical scalar values equal validator-produced scalar values under existing domain semantics. Reject unsupported physical-order lookup versions before I/O; assessment versions greater than 1 remain valid candidates.

orderAuthentication.lookup: candidate.order.id plus candidate.order.version; never current/latest fallback or caller-provided full order parameter
orderAuthentication.found: Run validateFoodPayableAssessmentAgainstOrder(candidate, authenticatedOrder); exact ID/version and merchandiseSubtotal currency/minorUnits must match.
orderAuthentication.notFound: invalid, zero assessment writes; align with current 008E dependency-failure mapping. Absence is not payment rejection.
orderAuthentication.validCandidateMismatch: invalid, zero assessment writes; this proposed API explicitly follows 008E rather than 008C's conflict mapping for invalid candidate/order relationships.
orderAuthentication.wrongCoordinatesOrMalformedOrderRow: storage-failure from 008B, never downgrade to invalid candidate or not-found
orderAuthentication.cancelledOrder: 005J's against-order validator does not restrict state. Permit a valid historical assessment bound to authenticated cancelled order version 2. This is historical evidence, not a presently collectable payable, refund, reinstatement or fulfillment authorization.
orderAuthentication.externalReferences: 005J validates opaque adjustment/provenance strings and its order snapshot without fetching price, tax-policy, SKU or payment records. Do not invent these retrieval dependencies. 005Q/005R and policy authentication remain separate.

validation.durableRows: Use exact six own-data columns, supported primitive versions/format and canonical full payload authentication. Read zero or one exact row using LIMIT 2; more than one, sparse/accessor array slots, unknown response success, missing/non-array results or unsafe stored content is storage-failure. D1 metadata is permitted only as safely captured envelope data; own success must be true and own results an actual supported array.
validation.predecessor: For an absent requested version n > 1, read exactly (same assessment ID, n-1), authenticate full snapshot/coordinates/canonical text, and reject missing predecessor as conflict. A structurally valid predecessor bound to different order coordinates is conflict without creating a success value. If coordinates match, validate predecessor against the exact authenticated order; a contradictory subtotal is corrupt durable state and storage-failure. Rebuild the expected candidate via reviseFoodPayableAssessmentVersion(previous, requested identity, authenticated order, candidate.adjustments, candidate.assessment) and require full canonical equality.
validation.existingDivergence: A structurally canonical row at the requested identity/version that differs from the candidate suffices for conflict; rejecting it does not authenticate a different order or grant authority to that divergent record. A success additionally requires exact candidate equality and against-order validation. Malformed/noncanonical content is storage-failure, not conflict.

publicApi.databaseSurface: Structurally compatible with 008B: prepare(sql).bind(...values).all<T>() returning Promise<{ readonly success: boolean; readonly results?: T[] }>. Only parameterized SELECT and one INSERT RETURNING. No transaction, exec, batch, session, run or provider capability required by this API.
publicApi.failures: No durable/partial value, raw row, SQL error, D1 metadata or provider reference fields on failures. Catch normal operational and hostile-input exceptions and return the contracted outcome.
publicApi.additionalPublicApis: None: no public exact read, list/history, latest/current, assessment selection, payment-status derivation, reconciliation or mutation API. Private predecessor reading is not a public read seam.

operationOrder: Capture, validate and detach candidate; canonicalize its complete snapshot; validate supported physical-order lookup coordinates. All malformed input exits invalid before D1.
Authenticate exact durable order via 008B on the same injected database; map its outcome and validate candidate against order. This precedes replay classification on every call.
Read the exact assessment ID/version using private exact SELECT, six explicit columns, both equality predicates and LIMIT 2.

If a canonical exact row exists, identical full canonical content plus exact order validation returns already-present without writing, even when later revisions exist. Valid divergent content returns conflict; unsafe storage returns storage-failure. Do not demand a predecessor or latest version for an already-recorded historical replay.

If absent and version > 1, authenticate exact predecessor n-1 and prove the transition through the existing revise function. Missing or different-order predecessor is conflict; corrupted storage is storage-failure. No query for greatest/latest/current assessment.
If absent and version = 1, no predecessor is required; its first-history condition is atomically enforced by the SQL initial guard. Do not infer new creation merely from a non-atomic precheck.

Attempt one ordinary INSERT of six captured column values in storage.columnsInOrder order with RETURNING those same explicit columns. DB guards and primary key must be installed. Never INSERT OR REPLACE, UPSERT or overwrite.

Only exactly one authenticated returned row equal to the requested canonical content yields created. A thrown prepare/bind/all operation, uncertain/malformed response, zero/multiple/mismatched returned rows or uniqueness/guard rejection triggers one exact identity recovery read.

After uncertainty, exact identical canonical row plus order validation returns already-present; exact canonical divergent row returns conflict; no row, malformed content, wrong coordinates, duplicate rows, thrown recovery read or unresolved state returns storage-failure. Never retry INSERT and never claim the first attempt did not persist merely from storage-failure.
Freeze the result wrapper and return newly reconstructed domain-owned frozen evidence only on success. Do not mutate caller, rows, order, previous assessment or any other authority.

privateSql.exactRead: SELECT assessment_id, assessment_version, order_id, order_version, snapshot_format_version, snapshot_json FROM food_payable_assessment_versions WHERE assessment_id = ? AND assessment_version = ? LIMIT 2
exactReadBindings: requested exact assessment version or exact predecessor version
privateSql.insert: INSERT INTO food_payable_assessment_versions (assessment_id, assessment_version, order_id, order_version, snapshot_format_version, snapshot_json) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) RETURNING assessment_id, assessment_version, order_id, order_version, snapshot_format_version, snapshot_json
privateSql.readBound: One exact order SELECT plus one requested-assessment SELECT; an absent revision adds one predecessor SELECT; uncertainty adds one requested-assessment recovery SELECT. Maximum four SELECTs and one mutation attempt. No recursive ancestor scan or public latest selection.

appendSemantics.historicalAuthority: Recording version n does not prove it is selected, usable, latest or currently collectable. A later n+1 never modifies n. No deadline, current date, accepted state or payer instruction is manufactured.

idempotency.differentVersion: Separate immutable row, requiring exact consecutive predecessor when not already present.
idempotency.sameKeyOtherOrder: conflict if the candidate first authenticates its own exact order and the existing row is structurally canonical; invalid candidate/order dependency takes precedence. No retargeting or merging.
idempotency.equivalence: Full canonical payload text after validated reconstruction, including assessment metadata, all money, order context and adjustment order. Equal amountDue alone is not equivalent. Opaque source references are not global idempotency keys.
idempotency.uncertainOutcome: Single exact reread classifies actual durable identity rather than retrying the write. already-present after a race does not identify which caller inserted the row. storage-failure does not prove rollback or absence.

concurrency.designStatus: Specified conditional guarantee; runtime race safety is not yet implemented or proven.
databaseGuaranteedWhenInstalled: A composite primary key permits at most one durable row per assessment identity/version.

BEFORE INSERT initial/revision/order guards execute within the same statement as insertion. Together with immutable history, they require a version-1 start, consecutive predecessor and stable order binding, even when earlier application reads race.
One INSERT stores the entire assessment aggregate; there is no independently committed adjustment child or mutable current pointer.
No-update/delete triggers preserve authenticated parent/predecessor content after successful reads under normal authorized schema operation.
adapterGuaranteedAfterProof: full row authentication and content comparison

concurrency.readConsistency: No multi-statement transaction, batch atomicity, sticky session or global linearizable read-after-write guarantee is assumed. failureSemantics.created: One inserted row returned and authenticated as exactly the requested canonical assessment after exact order and, for new revisions, predecessor validation.
failureSemantics.already-present: Requested complete canonical historical value is already durably recorded and authenticated; exact order is validated on this append call. No newest/current claim.
failureSemantics.conflict: Canonical key reused with different content, missing consecutive predecessor for a new revision, or stable assessment/order binding conflict. No business payment failure or policy rejection is inferred.
failureSemantics.invalid: Malformed/hostile/noncanonical candidate, invalid domain arithmetic/provenance, unsupported order coordinates, exact order not-found/invalid or candidate-versus-authentic-order mismatch. All prevent assessment writes.
failureSemantics.storage-failure: Operational read/write failure, malformed/uncertain D1 response, duplicate exact rows, corrupt durable row/JSON, coordinate mismatch, unsupported format, invalid predecessor content or unresolved insert result. This outcome does not assert no side effect occurred.
failureSemantics.precedence: Candidate validation, order authentication, requested identity classification, then new-revision prerequisite, then one insert/recovery. A malformed candidate cannot use conflict as a substitute for invalid; malformed durable content cannot be represented as not-found or already-present.
failureSemantics.exceptions: Do not propagate raw SQL/provider errors or partially reconstruct a success. Returned failure wrappers are frozen and carry only outcome.

securityBoundaries.recordsAreAssertions: assessedOn, attribution, sourceReference and adjustment provenance are caller-supplied domain facts. No existing 005J function authenticates the assessor, tax jurisdiction, discount entitlement or policy authorization. Recording structurally valid data cannot confer those authorities.
securityBoundaries.unauthorizedAdjustment: Malformed or duplicate-reference adjustments fail domain validation. A well-shaped adjustment lacking external policy authorization cannot be detected by this API and is persisted only as an assertion; later trusted policy/inclusion/selection gates remain mandatory. Do not claim persistence proves a charge is legally or operationally authorized.
securityBoundaries.querySafety: Static SQL and bound parameters only; no string interpolation of IDs, references or JSON into executable SQL. No toJSON or coercion hook from caller objects: serialize only explicitly constructed validated objects.
securityBoundaries.permissions: No HTTP handler, authentication bypass, public checkout endpoint, capability to run arbitrary SQL, provider access, payment references from other tables, clocks, randomness, filesystem runtime work, notifications or deployment.
securityBoundaries.operationalHistory: Cancelled order evidence remains historical. cancelled != refunded, reversed, released, stocked, paid or fulfilled. No effect is triggered by a zero amountDue or a reference label such as tax/delivery/discount.
